clue.text: Medal winner entered ahead of this

indicators.note: the winner's word is written in before the next piece, so it comes first

parts.note: a victor is one who wins
the clue itself sits at 1 across, so 'this' stands for the entry's own position, one across

explanation.surface: A list of honours where a medal winner's name has been written in before this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the clue's own slot in the grid: 1 across, read as I ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military gallantry award, a decoration of bronze.

clue.text: Unveil Dome's new sculpture

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is made by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, with its s

explanation.surface: A new statue is revealed under a dome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is a famous ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

clue.text: Vacated Côte-d'Or, and from France headed east to holiday island

indicators.note: the next piece is where it heads, so it is added on
emptied of its contents, leaving just the first and last letters

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves Burgundy and sets off eastward from France for an island break.
explanation.walkthrough: Côte-d'Or is a Burgundy wine region; emptied it leaves CR.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is a large Greek island and a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Make confused old boy melt, cuddling pet

indicators.note: the melt word wraps round the pet word as if hugging it

parts.note: to fuse is to melt
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: An elderly man goes soft and loses his wits while hugging his cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to confuse or make obscure.

clue.text: Receive knight in one hour, flag being raised

indicators.note: the knight's letter goes inside the pair for one and hour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tire is to flag

explanation.surface: Being knighted within the hour as a banner is hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but means tire, which 'being raised' reverses in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive something, typically from someone who has died.

clue.text: Caught famous prisoner in game

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy, was held for decades in Spandau prison

explanation.surface: A notable prisoner apprehended during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Hess flew to Scotland in 1941 and spent his final decades as Spandau's sole inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players.

clue.text: One starred as a snake handler — in his pouch, universal slithering

definitions.text: One starred as a snake handler

indicators.note: snakes slither in wriggling motion, so the letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: An actor playing a snake handler with a snake sliding about in his pouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starred' suggests acting, but it means made of stars: a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophiuchus is the constellation of the Serpent Bearer, depicted holding a snake.

clue.text: Runner up in Frederiksberg

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read backwards
the letters are found inside the place name

explanation.surface: A competitor finishing second in a Copenhagen district race.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederiksberg is a district of Copenhagen; inside it, IKS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, the long blade a sledge or skier glides on.

clue.text: Eager to put name forward for bender

indicators.note: N, the usual abbreviation for name, is shifted towards the front of the word

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: Someone keen to nominate a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put name forward' moves the N of KEEN up two places to give the new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint of the leg is what bends, so a cryptic 'bender' fits it.

clue.text: Physicist's in after explosion, storing hydrogen and helium separately

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A scientist caught up in the aftermath of a lab blast involving two gases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word but is part of the fodder; 'storing' and 'separately' say H and HE are added to INAFTER as two pieces before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was the German-born physicist who devised the temperature scale bearing his name.

clue.text: Judge is very much right on animals

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed on, that is after, the animals

parts.note: asses are donkeys, a kind of animal
so means very much, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is extremely correct about animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or judges, for instance a property's value or a claim.

clue.text: Queen sat in type of window for press

indicators.note: the queen's abbreviation sits inside the window word

parts.note: a sash is a sliding window

explanation.surface: A queen perched in a particular window frame, about to be squeezed.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash something is to press or crush it flat.

clue.text: After medal, pounds track

indicators.note: the pounds word comes after the medal word

parts.note: silver is a medal for second place
a stone is a weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Money spent after winning a medal on a race circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the British motor-racing circuit; a stone is the British weight unit of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverstone is a motor-racing track in Northamptonshire, home of the British Grand Prix.

clue.text: Literally, actress who reads the headlines?

parts.note: read letter by letter, 'new' signals an anagram and SCASTER is a fresh arrangement of the letters of actress

explanation.surface: An actress who has become a TV presenter, reading out the main news stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NEW SCASTER: 'new' is an anagram indicator and SCASTER rearranges ACTRESS, so the answer is wordplay for 'actress', which 'Literally' tells you.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreader on television or radio reads out the headlines.

clue.text: Deceitful person taking food and drink

parts.note: a snake in the grass is a treacherous person
a bite is a snack, a bit of food

explanation.surface: A liar helping themselves to refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: A snakebite is a British pub drink of lager and cider mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is a drink made of equal parts lager and cider.

clue.text: Breathe new life into cricket side, shortly to enter playing area at start of test

indicators.note: the shortened side goes into the playing area word

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Surrey is an English county cricket team

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word test is taken

explanation.surface: Reviving a cricket team by sending it out at the start of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county cricket side; a 'rec' is British slang for a public recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect is to bring back to life, to revive.

clue.text: Trim head and tail off cold pike

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word for cold are cut away

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a chilled fish by removing its head and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pike' looks like the fish, but in northern England a pike is a peaked hill, as in Scafell Pike.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Lake District a pike is a pointed summit, a kind of mountain or high ground.

clue.text: After violent impact, vehicle's front parts brought back for test

indicators.note: the collected letters are then read in reverse order
the initial letter of each of these four words is taken

explanation.surface: A car's front end being recovered after a crash, then checked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva, short for viva voce, is an oral exam, especially for a university degree.

clue.text: Use assets extravagantly, with unquantified amount for area that's down a lot

indicators.note: spending extravagantly throws things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
x stands for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Advice against squandering one's wealth on an indefinite sum.
explanation.walkthrough: EAST SUSSEX is an English county on the south coast; much of it lies on the South Downs, chalk hills, hence 'down a lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Downs chalk hills cover much of this southern English county, so it is full of downland.

clue.text: Covering severe criticism

definitions.meaning: roofing tiles of stone laid as a roof's outer layer
a harsh attack or panning, as in a bad review

explanation.definitionFit: Slating is both roofing material and a harsh critical review.

clue.text: Jacket potato at last served to cricketer with fall of wicket

indicators.note: the potato's letter is handed over to follow the cricketer piece
the wicket's letter drops out of the cricketer word

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: the final letter of the word potato is used

explanation.surface: A baked potato handed to a cricketer just as a wicket falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket, worn by men in Spain or by women over a dress.

clue.text: Director-general's heart given to article in periodical

indicators.note: the article is added on to the first piece
the central letters of the compound word are taken

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The head of a broadcaster contributing a piece to a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central three letters of DIRECTORGENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a group, as in a house organ.

clue.text: Sort of spray making lock smoother, commonly

indicators.note: in common or Cockney speech the initial h is dropped

parts.note: a hairbrush smooths locks of hair

explanation.surface: A spray product that helps smooth out one's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' imitates the dropped h of Cockney speech, so the brush loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbrush sprays paint with compressed air, so it is a kind of spraying device.

clue.text: Dance group regularly put on business course

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the next
every other letter of the word group is taken

parts.note: an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A band who regularly take a business degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Following single, go round boundary where you're subject to 19

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
to ring is to encircle, to go round
a line marks a boundary

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: after a single, a batsman goes round to the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is SLATING, severe criticism; in the firing line you bear the brunt of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the firing line means being the target of attack or criticism.

clue.text: Prepared tongue — tell me you want some?

definitions.meaning: an artificial language devised from Esperanto
the reply of someone saying yes, they'd like it

explanation.definitionFit: Ido is a constructed language, and 'I do' is a yes answer to an offer.

clue.text: Feeling of judgment from the far right?

indicators.note: read starting at the right-hand end, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: doom means judgment, as in Doomsday

explanation.surface: A political sentiment coming from extreme right-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far right' suggests politics, but here it means read from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is a state of feeling or emotion.

clue.text: Bag a two-day hearing?

definitions.meaning: a small suitcase for a one-night stay
a court case that runs over a night, spanning two days

explanation.definitionFit: An overnight case is a small piece of luggage, and a trial adjourned overnight is also one.
